brands.name: HP
brands.overview: HP makes four of the lines we sell: EliteBook (premium business), ProBook (mid-range business), ZBook (mobile workstations with dedicated graphics) and Elite x2 (a detachable tablet). Start with the series that fits your budget.

series.name: HP EliteBook
series.knownFor: HP's premium business line: metal build, a good keyboard and easy to service. The 830 is 13.3-inch, the 840 and 845 are 14-inch, a model number ending in 5 (745, 845) means an AMD Ryzen chip, and x360 models fold back into a tablet.
advice: For everyday office work the 840 G6 and 830 G6 are the value picks: 8th Gen chips that run Windows 11, for less than the G7 and G8.
If you keep many apps and tabs open, choose a 16GB configuration or the AMD 845 G8.
For presenting, signing documents or taking notes, the x360 830 models flip into a tablet.
The 840 G3 and G4 are the cheapest way into an EliteBook, but their 6th and 7th Gen chips can't officially run Windows 11.

faq.q: What does the G number on an EliteBook mean?
faq.a: It is the generation. On the 830 and 840: G3 has a 6th Gen Intel chip, G4 7th Gen, G5 and G6 8th Gen, G7 10th Gen and G8 11th Gen. A higher G is newer and faster.

faq.q: What's the difference between the EliteBook 840 and 845?
faq.a: They share the same 14-inch design. The 840 uses an Intel processor; the 845 (like the 745) uses an AMD Ryzen processor, which is strong at multitasking.

series.name: HP ProBook
series.knownFor: HP's mid-range business line: the same practical design as the EliteBook at a lower price. The 450 is the big-screen 15.6-inch option with a number pad, and the x360 11 is a tough convertible made for school.
advice: The 440 G8 has the newest chip in the range (11th Gen) at a mid-range price.
The 450 G7 suits anyone who wants a bigger screen and plenty of file space: an SSD plus a 1TB hard drive, and 2GB graphics.
The x360 11 G5 is for school work, browsing and video calls, not heavy software.

faq.q: ProBook or EliteBook: which should I buy?
faq.a: EliteBook is HP's premium line, with better materials and screens. ProBook is the mid-range line. For the same money a ProBook is usually a newer generation, so compare the processor generation, not just the name.

faq.q: Which ProBook has the biggest screen?
faq.a: The ProBook 450 G7, with a 15.6-inch screen and a number pad.

series.name: HP ZBook
series.knownFor: HP's mobile workstations: slim 14-inch laptops with dedicated NVIDIA graphics for CAD, design and video editing.
advice: The Firefly 14 G8 is the most powerful laptop we list: 11th Gen i7, 32GB of RAM and 4GB graphics.
The Firefly 14 G6 is the lower-cost way into dedicated graphics, with a touchscreen.

faq.a: Only if your software leans on the graphics card: CAD, 3D, design or video editing. For Office, browsing and video calls an EliteBook costs less and does the job.

series.name: HP Elite x2
series.knownFor: A 12-inch Windows tablet with a detachable keyboard, light enough to carry like a notebook.
advice: Choose the 8GB / 256GB unit for everyday use.
The 4GB unit comes with a pen; it suits note-taking and light use rather than heavy multitasking.

faq.q: Is the Elite x2 a tablet or a laptop?
faq.a: Both. It is a Windows tablet; attach the keyboard and it works like a small laptop.

series.name: Lenovo ThinkPad
series.knownFor: Lenovo's business line, known for its keyboards and the red TrackPoint. X models are small (12.5 to 13.3 inch), T models are the mainstream 14-inch line, X1 is the premium flagship, and Yoga models flip over into a tablet.
advice: The X13 Gen 1 is the standout value: a 10th Gen chip and 16GB of RAM.
The T490s suits power users: i7, 16GB, 512GB and a touchscreen.
The X260 and X270 are the cheapest, small and tough, but they stay on Windows 10.
Want a pen and tablet mode? Look at the Yoga models; several come with a stylus.

faq.q: What does "Yoga" mean on a ThinkPad?
faq.a: The screen folds all the way back, so the laptop works as a tablet for notes, signing documents and presenting.

faq.q: What are the X, T and X1 lines?
faq.a: X models are the small, light ThinkPads; T models are the mainstream 14-inch line; X1 is the premium flagship.

series.name: Dell Latitude
series.knownFor: Dell's business line. The 5000 series is mainstream and the 7000 series premium, and the second digit is roughly the screen size: the 5300 is 13-inch, the 5400 14-inch and the 7280 12-inch.
advice: The Latitude 5300 i5 is one of the cheapest laptops here that runs Windows 11.
The 5400 adds a 14-inch touchscreen.
The 7280 is the smallest; its processor generation varies, so check Windows 11 support with us for the exact unit.

faq.q: Which Latitude is best for a student?
faq.a: The Latitude 5300: 13-inch, light, and an 8th Gen chip that runs Windows 11.

series.name: Apple MacBook Pro
series.knownFor: Apple's 13-inch MacBook Pro, for people who need macOS.
advice: The 2018 models get the newest macOS versions of the three.
The 2017 model is a cheaper way into a Retina-screen MacBook Pro.
The 2012 model is the cheapest way into macOS, for writing, browsing and light work.

faq.q: Which macOS version can each MacBook Pro run?
faq.a: According to Apple, the 13-inch 2012 model's newest supported version is macOS Catalina, and the 13-inch 2018 four-port model supports macOS Sequoia. Ask us for the version installed on the exact unit.

series.name: HP EliteDesk & ProDesk Mini
series.knownFor: HP's business mini desktops: the EliteDesk 800 and ProDesk 600 G1 Mini share one compact chassis that tucks behind a monitor.
advice: Good for office, cyber café and point-of-sale use. Add your own monitor, keyboard and mouse.

faq.a: Not officially: its 4th Gen Intel chip is below the Windows 11 requirement.

series.name: Lenovo ThinkCentre
series.knownFor: Lenovo's palm-sized business desktop, the ThinkCentre M73 Tiny.
advice: Made for reception desks, cyber cafés and point-of-sale counters. Plug in a monitor, keyboard and mouse.

faq.a: Not officially: its 4th Gen Intel chip is below the Windows 11 requirement.
